result.summary: This is a move-only refactor that extracts legacy wallet migration code out of the 4500-line wallet.cpp into new wallet/migration.cpp and wallet/migration.h files, and also moves some utility functions into walletutil.cpp/h. It renames wallet/migrate.{cpp,h} to legacybdb.{cpp,h} to avoid a name clash with the new migration.cpp. No behavior change is intended; it is purely reorganizational.
result.problem: wallet/wallet.cpp is widely acknowledged as too large and hard to reason about, which slows down anyone trying to review or modify wallet code, especially around legacy-to-descriptor migration and the eventual goal of making the core wallet file descriptor-specific.

resolved_concerns: pablomartin4btc suggested a dedicated migration class for future migration types beyond legacy-to-descriptor; author explained migration is a one-off event and declined, with no further pushback

categories.evidence: Directly restructures src/wallet/wallet.cpp, wallet.h, walletutil.cpp/h, and creates wallet/migration.cpp/h and legacybdb.cpp/h, moving ~800 lines of legacy migration logic out of the core wallet file.
categories.rationale: This is a stated move-only refactor with no behavior change: 'many developers have noted that wallet/wallet.cpp is quite hard to reason about' (author). It has some leverage value by making the file more approachable for future descriptor-focused work, but it fixes no bug, adds no feature, and improves no fund safety or performance directly, so it sits in the worthwhile-but-deferrable band per the cleanup carve-out for internally focused changes.

uncertainties: Whether the move-only claim is fully accurate was not independently verified beyond the diff summary and commit messages; large omitted hunks in migration.cpp/wallet.cpp were not shown in full.
No second reviewer has substantively engaged beyond the Concept ACK, so broader maintainer appetite for this scale of refactor is unclear.
result.card: This PR is a pure move-only refactor extracting ~800 lines of legacy wallet migration code out of wallet/wallet.cpp into new wallet/migration.cpp and wallet/migration.h files, and renames wallet/migrate.{cpp,h} to legacybdb.{cpp,h} to avoid naming collision. The stated problem is that wallet.cpp, at over 4500 lines, is widely considered hard to reason about, and this shortens it while isolating legacy-specific code so the main file can eventually become descriptor-focused. It has one Concept ACK from pablomartin4btc with no objections, and a minor design suggestion (a dedicated migration class) was declined by the author without pushback. The PR has been kept rebased against master for roughly six months through 20 force-pushes, remains in clean mergeable state, and is ready for review with the author's suggested --color-moved=dimmed-zebra diff option. There is no dependency blocking it, though it conflicts textually with several other open wallet PRs touching the same files.
